result.title: When to Trust Adaptation: Contextual Fusion for Transferable Vision-Language Prompting
result.summary: When a vision-language model encounters a new class or domain, how much should it trust its learned prompts? Because source adaptation can correct pretrained errors on some target images while disturbing valid predictions on others, we introduce Contextual Adaptive Fusion (CAF), which retains four prediction branches by pairing frozen and prompted visual and textual representations. To arbitrate when branches disagree on an image, CAF combines each branch's predictive confidence with how frequently the branches favor its proposed class across the unlabeled target collection, placing greater trust in predictions that are locally confident yet less dominated by collection-wide frequency bias. The fusion coefficients are learned once on source data and remain fixed at inference. Trained on ImageNet, CAF achieves 69.96% average accuracy across ten cross-dataset benchmarks (1.92 percentage points above ManiPT) and remains highly competitive across four ImageNet variants, setting a new best of 52.21% on ImageNet-S. In base-to-novel transfer across eleven datasets, CAF further reaches 79.77% novel-class accuracy and an 82.81% harmonic mean. Code is available at https://github.com/zhenyuanchenai/CAF.

AI.brief_summary: 论文关注视觉语言模型遇到新类或新域时应在多大程度上信任已学提示，提出 Contextual Adaptive Fusion：把冻结与提示化的视觉、文本表示配成四个预测分支，按各分支的预测置信度及该分支在无标签目标集上偏向某类的频率来仲裁分歧，融合系数在源域学一次后固定。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「局部置信度 vs 集合级频率偏置」的分支仲裁与源域固定融合权重，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据分支与语言先验的加权、避免单一路径主导推理状态提供可供核查的线索；但本文不做 latent 推理，也无推理状态，迁移价值需自行判断。
